chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the woman in postnatal bleeding: how long does she refrain? He said: “Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays experienced postnatal bleeding, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله commanded her to perform ghusl on the eighteenth day; so there is no harm if she takes an extra precaution of a day or two.”

And this also indicates that he commanded her to perform ghusl on the eighteenth day, and it does not indicate that if she had informed him of a period less than that, he would have said the same to her.

Then he said—may Allah Most High support him—and likewise, if the menstruating woman sees blood on the eleventh day from the beginning of her menses, she performs ghusl after ensuring cessation and after wudu, and she prays and fasts; for that is the blood of istiḥāḍah and not menstruation, according to what we have stated previously.
Its explanation has already passed in what preceded, and in that there is sufficiency, if Allah wills.

key_terms.تَسْتَظْهِرَ: to take an extra precautionary period
key_terms.تَغْتَسِلَ: to perform ghusl, the ritual bath
key_terms.نُفِسَتْ: she experienced postnatal bleeding after childbirth

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on postnatal bleeding and blood seen after the tenth day of menstruation in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal rulings of postnatal bleeding and menstruation, citing the case of Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays and the instruction of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding ghusl on the eighteenth day. It also states that blood seen after the tenth day of menstruation is treated as istiḥāḍah, requiring purification and permitting salat and sawm.
